spec.name: Blend v33
spec.notes: Combined signal, rebalanced on a slow schedule.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.7, annual return 10%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.66 to 0.01 (change -2.65). The strategy already trades a bar after its signal, so this measures how fast the signal fades, not look-ahead.
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.66 to 2.66. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is -0.49 (as submitted, 0 bps: 2.66); it breaks even at 8.4 bps with daily turnover 0.49.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.66 against 2.66 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is -1.65 against 2.66 in research, a gap of +4.31.
The best year gives 20% of total P&L (year 8) and calm regimes give 77%; Sharpe is 3.11 in calm and 2.01 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 4 distinct specs; the best of 4 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.22, so the claimed 2.70 becomes 2.48 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.62 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.01, 95th percentile 0.55).
Perturbing the 3 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.66 to as low as 2.14 (as low as 2.51 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 23% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 12% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (cost_test EX-3, holdout_test EX-5).
